# Figure captions (generated by make_figures.py from results/results_sheet.csv)

**fig01_coverage_timeline.** Daily data coverage of the three rooms across the study. One tile marks a calendar day (flock age, days since placement on 5 June 2025) on which the modality contributed at least one observed hour; blank space is a day without any observation. Rows per room: morphometry (after the scale-artefact quality-control filter), spatial behaviour (tracking), optical flow and audio. Daily tiles preserve gaps. Hours from placement to each room's last observed hour (sheet S01): room 2 4,366, room 6 4,366, room 7 4,366. The three rooms are replicates within one flock and one production cycle. No inferential interval is shown.

**fig02_audio_calibration.** Comparison of raw RMS acoustic level trajectories showing cross-room calibration offsets versus within-room robust normalized mid-band energy fractions. Each line is the 5-day centred rolling mean of the daily median of the hourly feature, per room, against flock age.

**fig03_pipeline_overview.** Processing pipeline. Overhead camera video is converted to morphometric, spatial-behaviour (flock spacing and movement) and optical-flow features with YOLOv11 detection and Bytetrack tracking; room audio is converted with a short-time Fourier transform to call-structure and call-level features. Features are calibrated across rooms, aligned to the hour, fused at feature level and passed to a histogram-based gradient-boosted regression-tree estimator, which yields developmental age, SHAP modality attribution and the growth-deviation gap.

**fig04_loro_predicted_vs_true.** Predicted versus actual flock age for the fused model under leave-one-room-out validation. (a) Windows with usable features. (b) All evaluated windows; grey points are windows whose trailing 6 h contained fewer than three observed hours (723 of 4,198; 17.2%). An anchor hour can have all required sensor streams present and still lack enough observations in its six-hour window to compute temporal features. Reported metrics are computed on all windows. Each point is one 6 h evaluation window of the held-out room (model trained on the other two rooms), coloured by room; the dashed line is perfect prediction. Legend entries give each room's mean absolute error (MAE, days) on the windows shown in the panel. The three rooms are replicates within one flock and one cycle; no interval is drawn on the scatter (intervals for these errors are in Fig 8 and are conditional on this cohort and these rooms). MAE = mean absolute error.

**fig05_model_family_comparison.** Comparison of model families under leave-one-room-out validation on the primary pipeline (same features, folds, seed and 4,198 complete-case 6 h windows for every model). (a) Mean absolute error and (b) R² (clipped at −1; unclipped value printed), each the mean of the three held-out rooms. Dark blue: the reported HistGradientBoosting model, which uses all window scales and handles missing values natively; mid blue: other regressor families (all on the 6 h evaluation windows only; median imputation, and standardisation where the model needs it, were fitted on the two training rooms and applied to the held-out room); red: other model classes — a Gompertz growth-curve inversion of relative body height (scored only on windows with the size feature, n = 3,475), an ordinal three-stage classifier (predicted age = fixed stage centres) and a GRU over 24 h sequences (mean of 5 seeds, MAE range 14.7–21.1 d, scored on its own 4,132 anchors rather than the 4,198 windows). Imputation and scaling of each model, and HGB without window augmentation (18.5 d, not drawn), are listed in the sheet (section S32). Hyperparameters are fixed for every model; none was tuned. Conditional on this cohort and these three rooms (n = 3 folds); no interval is drawn. MAE = mean absolute error.

**fig06_attribution_by_modality.** Attribution of the primary fused model's predictions to feature blocks across age bands. For every held-out 6 h window, the absolute SHAP values of all columns in a block were summed and divided by the total; shares are the mean over windows within each age band, then the mean over the three held-out rooms (leave-one-room-out). (a) Stacked shares of all six blocks. (b) The three largest groups; labels give the morphometry share. 'Attribution' denotes the share of total absolute SHAP value, not a causal effect. Conditional on this cohort and these three rooms (n = 3 folds); the range across rooms is in the sheet (section S21). SHAP = SHapley Additive exPlanations.

**fig07_feature_attribution.** Twenty columns with the largest attribution in the primary fused model under leave-one-room-out validation. Bars give the mean absolute SHAP value (in days of predicted age) over the held-out 6 h windows, averaged over the three rooms. Colour marks the feature block; '(level)' is the window mean of the feature and '(rate of change)' its slope over the window. Names follow the feature dictionary. 'Attribution' denotes mean absolute SHAP value, not a causal effect. Conditional on this cohort and these three rooms (n = 3 folds). SHAP = SHapley Additive exPlanations.

**fig08_error_by_growth_phase.** Mean absolute error by developmental phase (growth, true age ≤ 70 d; plateau, > 70 d) for the six feature sets, under leave-one-room-out validation (primary pipeline). Bars are the mean over the three held-out rooms of each room's MAE (days) in the phase; the fused model's phases contain 850 (growth) and 3,348 (plateau) 6 h windows. No interval is drawn on the bars; 95% room-day bootstrap intervals for the fused, morphometry-only, V3 and V2 models are in sheet section S27 and the paired differences in sheet section S07. Conditional on this cohort and these rooms. MAE = mean absolute error.

**fig09_body_size_trajectory.** Body-size trajectory of the three rooms. Each line is the daily median of the relative median body height (after the causal scale-artefact filter) divided by the median of the room's first seven observed daily medians, so every room starts at 1. The mean over rooms of the peak ratio (maximum of the 7-day centred rolling median) is 2.01. The dashed line marks day 70. Rooms differ in the size of the trajectory (the between-room difference is in sheet section S36), so the morphometric features are referenced to each room's own first week. Descriptive; conditional on this cohort and these three rooms.

**fig10_clustering_crossover.** Unsupervised two-phase structure of the fused feature space, one panel per room. Each room was clustered separately (median imputation, within-room standardisation, 20 principal components, k-means with k = 2, seed 0) using only the sensor feature window means of the primary pipeline's complete-case 6 h windows; age, date and time of day were withheld. The line is the share of hours assigned to the cluster with the younger median age as a function of age (centred 7-day rolling mean of the daily share). Dashed line: the pre-registered 50% crossing (first age after day 35 at which the smoothed share falls below 0.5); dash-dotted line: the sustained crossing (the share stays below 0.5 for 3 consecutive days); dotted blue line: the supervised day-70 boundary. Panel text gives the k = 2 silhouette and the two crossing days, which equal the values in the tables (asserted in code); the 50% crossings of the three rooms span 62–74 d. The two-phase structure is clear in rooms 2 and 6 and weaker in room 7 (silhouette favours more than two clusters there; sheet S23). This is descriptive corroboration, not an interval estimate; conditional on this cohort and these three rooms.

**fig11_gap_recovery.** Recovery of synthetic age substitution by the calibrated detector. For every held-out 6 h anchor with an observation k days earlier at the same hour of day, the model was fed the sensor readings from k days earlier (all sensor blocks, or morphometry only) while the label stayed today's age; the detected gap is predicted minus true age after a bias correction fitted on the two training rooms only (inner calibration). Points are the median gap of trailing 7-calendar-day windows (valid with at least 4 days of data), error bars are 95% intervals from a room-week block bootstrap (2,000 resamples), conditional on this cohort and these three rooms. The 0 d point is the unperturbed run on all eligible anchors; the dashed line is perfect recovery (gap = −k). Window counts and weeks per room are in sheet section S28. (a) growth phase (age ≤ 70 d); (b) plateau phase (> 70 d).

**fig12_ageblock_predicted_vs_true.** (a, c) leave-one-age-block-out and (b, d) leave-one-room-out validation. Top row: windows with usable features. Bottom row: all evaluated windows; grey points are windows whose trailing 6 h contained fewer than three observed hours (723 of 4,198; 17.2%). Reported metrics are computed on all windows. Predicted against true flock age for the primary fused model (12 h embargo; windows reading any observation inside the held-out block or its embargo were removed from training). The age range of the complete-case windows was divided into five blocks (quintiles of age, B1–B5; boundaries from the fold manifest); each block was held out in turn and the model, trained on the remaining blocks of all three rooms, predicted its 6 h windows. Colour marks backward extrapolation (B1), internal gaps (B2–B4) and forward extrapolation (B5); the dashed segments mark the nearest training age for B1 and B5; labels above the panels give each block's MAE (days) on the windows shown. Panel MAE in (a, c) is the unweighted mean of the five block values; in (b, d) it is the mean over the three held-out rooms, with the matching R². Points in (b, d) are coloured by held-out room; the dashed line is perfect prediction. No interval is drawn: blocks and rooms are not replicates, and any interval would be conditional on this cohort and these rooms. MAE = mean absolute error.

**fig13a_confusion_room2.** Three-stage classification of flock age under leave-one-room-out validation: held-out Room 2. Stages are fixed age classes: brooding/early (0–60 d), growing (60–110 d) and mature (110–200 d). A cumulative-binary gradient-boosting classifier was trained on the 6 h windows of two rooms and applied to the third. Cells show the proportion of true-stage windows (rows sum to 1) and, in brackets, the number of windows. Balanced accuracy (mean of the three per-class recalls) is 0.668, macro-F1 (unweighted mean of the three per-class F1 scores) is 0.696, and 1,372 windows were evaluated. No interval is shown: the rooms are the replicates, and any interval would be conditional on this cohort and these rooms. F1 = harmonic mean of precision and recall.

**fig14_negative_controls.** Final reported models and negative controls under leave-one-room-out validation (primary pipeline; all numbers from the results sheet). Bars give (a) the mean absolute error and (b) R² (clipped at −1; unclipped value printed), each the mean over the three held-out rooms. Blue: the fused, video-only, morphometry-only and audio-only models. Red: thermal diagnostics that expose calendar leakage (a house-wide thermal trace joined to every room by timestamp predicts age through the calendar, not through the birds; thermal rows are means over folds and seeds). Grey: negative controls — a thermal trace assigned at random, the median-body-height baseline, hour of day only, sensor health only, the global-mean baseline, the shuffled-label control (age labels of the two training rooms permuted as whole room-day blocks; mean of 100 permutations) and seasonal extrapolation (summer = age < 88 d, 12 h embargo; the summer-held-out fold has no relative-morphometry features). Conditional on this cohort and these three rooms. MAE = mean absolute error.
